issue.title: Antigravity registry still offers retired gemini-3.5-flash slugs that agy models no longer returns
issue.description:
SASE's Antigravity registry advertises three Gemini 3.5 Flash slugs that Antigravity
no longer serves, so the ACE model picker, `%model` completion, and provider-scoped
`agy/` completion all offer models that `agy --model` will reject.

`llm_known_model_names()` in `src/sase/llm_provider/agy.py` is documented as the
"exact stable slugs reported by `agy models`", but the live catalog has since dropped
the whole 3.5 Flash family (and gained 3.8 Flash). Found while planning the Gemini 3.8
Flash catalog addition, which deliberately left this untouched because removing catalog
entries is a user-reaching removal that needs its own deprecation decision, not an
additive change.

Deciding how to remove them is part of the work: a straight delete breaks provider
inference for anyone whose prompts or configs still say `%m:agy/gemini-3.5-flash-high`
or `gemini-3.5-flash-*`, so consider whether a model advisory
(`llm_model_advisories()`), a deprecation window, or a plain removal is right. The same
staleness will recur on every Antigravity catalog rotation, so a cheap parity check
worth considering is a doctor check or an opt-in test that diffs
`llm_known_model_names()` against `agy --output-format json models` when the CLI is
installed.

Also update `llm_model_short_aliases()` (`flash35h`/`flash35m`/`flash35l`), the
Antigravity rows of the provider-resolution and shorthand tables in `docs/llms.md`, and
the tests that pin the exact catalog and alias map
(`tests/llm_provider/test_agy_provider_core.py`, `tests/test_llm_provider_core.py`,
`tests/test_agy_integration_polish.py`, `tests/test_model_picker_modal.py`, and
`tests/test_directives_split_models_naming.py` all reference 3.5 slugs).

task_type_fields.impact: Anyone who picks a Gemini 3.5 Flash row in the ACE model picker or completes it via %model gets a slug Antigravity will reject at launch. Low blast radius (3.5 is two families old) but it is a broken affordance SASE presents as valid, and it will recur on every Antigravity catalog rotation.
task_type_fields.repro:
Run the live catalog query and diff it against SASE's static registry:

```bash
agy --output-format json models   # command.data.models[*].id -> 14 ids, no gemini-3.5-*
python -c "from sase.llm_provider.agy import AgyProvider; print(AgyProvider().llm_known_model_names())"
```

On 2026-09-04 with agy 1.1.26 the live ids were gemini-3.8-flash-{high,medium,low},
gemini-3.7-flash-{high,medium,low}, gemini-3.6-flash-{high,medium,low},
gemini-3.1-pro-{high,low}, claude-sonnet-4-6, claude-opus-4-6-thinking, and
gpt-oss-120b-medium. SASE still returns gemini-3.5-flash-{high,medium,low}. Typing
`gemini-3.5` into the ACE model picker filter, or completing `%m:agy/`, offers all three.
